usageNotes: Issues an immediate hard stop of a remote LXC container — equivalent to pulling power, with no graceful shutdown sequence. Use this only when a clean shutdown via the 'shutdown' endpoint is not possible (e.g., container is frozen or unresponsive). Returns a remote UPID string; poll the remote task status endpoint to confirm completion. Requires Resource.Manage on the container's resource path.

examples.summary: Force-stop LXC container 102 on a named remote

destructiveReason: Immediately kills the container process without flushing disk buffers or running shutdown hooks, which can cause filesystem corruption or data loss for in-flight writes.
tips: Prefer the 'shutdown' endpoint for any container with active write workloads; use 'stop' only when shutdown is unresponsive.
The 'node' body param is optional — omit it to let PDM resolve the node automatically from the remote cluster.
Track the returned UPID against the remote task API to confirm the stop completed before attempting start or migration operations.
